summary:
Replay the evening with a real stack. Push the washed plates in order; whenever the top is the next plate to
serve, take it at once (waiting never helps: the plate can only get buried). It could happen exactly when every
plate gets served. O(n).

question.md:
Plates are stacked in `washed` order, and at any moment a waiter can take the top plate. Given the order they
were served, could that order have happened?

- **Pushes follow `washed` exactly**, but pops can be interleaved anywhere.
- **Every plate is pushed once and served once**, and all numbers are distinct.
- **Up to 10⁵ plates.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Plates can be served immediately after washing, or wait at any depth.
- Numbers are distinct, so each serve matches exactly one plate.
- Served order equal to washed order is always possible.

think.md:
**Let new items collide with the top.** In these processes a new item only ever interacts with the **most recent
survivors**: the comet just to its left, the truck just ahead, the plate on top. A stack holds the survivors so far,
and each new item fights the top until it either wins (pop and continue) or stops. Every item is pushed and popped at
most once: O(n).

**Replay greedily.** Wash plates in order; after each wash, serve from the top as long as the top is the next
plate to be served. Serving as early as possible never hurts: a plate that's on top and due now can only block
others if it stays. If all plates get served, the order was possible. Washed `[3, 1, 4, 2, 5]`, served `[1, 4, 2, 5, 3]`:
Stuck with plates left on the stack: **false**.

approaches.title: Check the reverse-order rule for every plate

idea.md:
Use the rule that characterises stack orders: after serving plate `p`, any plates washed **before** `p`
and served later must come out in reverse washing order. Check it for every plate with a scan of the rest.

build: Washing position of every served plate.
For each plate, scan later serves.
Plates washed earlier must appear in decreasing washing order.

lines.text: Translate each served plate into its washing position (when it was pushed).
Take the plate served at step `j`; `last` tracks the most recent position seen below it.
Plates served later but washed earlier were under `served[j]` when it left. Walk them in serving order.
Their positions must decrease (newest-washed leaves first). An increase means a plate had to come out from under another one.
Every plate passed: the order is possible.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** (plus O(n²) for the `index` lookups). **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Serve 1. Plates washed before it and served later: [3]. Their washing positions [0] decrease, so the order works.
Serve 4. Plates washed before it and served later: [3]. Their washing positions [0] decrease, so the order works.
Serve 2. Plates washed before it and served later: [3]. Their washing positions [0] decrease, so the order works.
Serve 5. Plates washed before it and served later: [3]. Their washing positions [0] decrease, so the order works.
Serve 3. Plates washed before it and served later: none.
Every plate passes the rule: it could happen.

walk.title: Rule: when a plate is served, every plate washed before it and still unserved is in the stack below it, and those must come out newest-washed first.

limits.md: Quadratic. Simply replaying with a stack checks the same rule in one pass.

approaches.title: Replay with a stack

idea.md: Push each washed plate, then pop while the top is the next plate to serve. Possible exactly when every plate was served.

build: Empty stack and a pointer into `served`.
Check the pointer reached the end.

lines.text: The plate stack and `j`, the next plate that must be served.
Wash the next plate onto the stack.

If the top is the plate that must go next, serve it now; waiting would only bury it. Repeat, since the plate below might be next too. `j` can't run past the end: once all plates are served the stack is empty.
Possible exactly when every plate got served.

steps.text: The top is 1, the next plate to serve: take it now.
The top is 4, the next plate to serve: take it now.
The top is 2, the next plate to serve: take it now.
The top is 5, the next plate to serve: take it now.
The top is 3, the next plate to serve: take it now.
All 5 plates were served in order: it could happen.

walk.title: Replay with a real stack: push each washed plate, and whenever the top is the next plate to serve, serve it immediately.

takeaways.md:
- **Validate a stack sequence:** replay it, popping greedily whenever the top matches.
- Greedy is safe because waiting can only block later plates.
- **Pitfall:** checking only that each served plate was washed before it's served.
